positive: Verify one index per distinct expression value and that each returned index maps to the represented value.

edge: Use all-equal and all-distinct arrays.
notes: Do not assert a particular result order or representative among duplicates.
positive: Use repeated values and a with expression mapping distinct elements to duplicate keys; compare result as an unordered set.

edge: Vary only the slowest dimension kind.
negative: Use differing element types, fixed target counts, dimension counts, or faster-dimension types.
positive: Assign between fixed, dynamic, and queue outer dimensions with equivalent nested element types.

edge: Use nonzero and negative bounds.
positive: Assign equal-size arrays with opposite index directions and verify leftmost-to-leftmost correspondence.

edge: Use an unpacked array as the element type.
negative: Place an intended unpacked range before the identifier.
positive: Declare an unpacked array of structures and a multidimensional unpacked array.

edge: Compare element signedness with whole-array assignment behavior.
positive: Declare an unpacked array of signed packed elements and verify signed element arithmetic.

edge: Nest unpacked arrays around a packed element.
positive: Declare unpacked arrays of scalar, packed-array, and unpacked-array elements.

edge: Use the mandated minimum element count.
notes: Materialization may require compile-only resource-conscious handling.
positive: Declare a fixed-size unpacked array containing exactly 16777216 scalar elements.

negative: Declare an unpacked struct signed.
positive: Declare an unpacked struct without a signing qualifier.

edge: Use a one-member common prefix.
negative: Inspect beyond the equivalent initial prefix.
positive: Put one of two structures sharing initial member types into a union and inspect the shared prefix through the other.

edge: Use a first member with a 4-state integral type.
positive: Declare an unpacked union with no initializer and observe the first member's type default.

edge: Combine empty/null elements with otherwise valid nested fields.
positive: Use aggregate keys containing empty strings, empty arrays, or null handles.

edge: Add or delete a key, after which relative order may change for a nonrelational type.
notes: Do not require the arbitrary order to match across runs or tools.
positive: Traverse unchanged keys repeatedly within one run and verify stable order; test a relationally ordered type separately.

edge: Place the unknown in a deeply nested element.
negative: Use an aggregate key with a nested X or Z bit.
positive: Use a fully known aggregate key.

edge: Assign an empty source.
positive: Assign shorter and longer source arrays to dynamic arrays and queues.

edge: Pass any one-dimensional unpacked string array to a string dynamic-array formal.
negative: Pass an incompatible element type, dimension count, or associative array.
positive: Pass each compatible actual kind to dynamic and queue formals.

edge: Use a zero-size source and zero-element-compatible context if available.
negative: Assign a shorter and a longer dynamic array or queue to a fixed target and verify the target is unchanged with an error.
notes: The diagnostic wording is not part of the oracle.
positive: Assign a runtime-sized source whose count matches the fixed target.

negative: Declare a void member in a struct or untagged union.
positive: Declare a void member in a tagged union.

edge: Use an integral index wider than 64 bits.
negative: Use a string or class expression as a wildcard index.
positive: Index one wildcard associative array with integral expressions of several widths and signednesses.

edge: Use ordinary integral indexed access on the same wildcard array as a legal control.
negative: Use foreach on a wildcard-index associative array.
positive: Use foreach with a typed associative array.

edge: Distinguish methods returning element values from methods returning indices.
negative: Invoke an index-returning locator method on a wildcard associative array.
positive: Use a value-returning manipulation method that does not return indices, where otherwise legal.

edge: Use zero and values whose high significant bit is one.
positive: Index with equal positive numeric values expressed at different widths and verify they address the same entry.

edge: Contrast a string literal, which has a specified conversion, with a string variable.
negative: Index it with real or class-handle expressions.
positive: Index a wildcard array with integral expressions.

edge: Mix key expression widths.
positive: Insert keys out of order and traverse with first/next to verify ascending numerical order.

edge: Use a signed negative expression and inspect its self-determined bit representation.
positive: Use the same bit pattern from signed and unsigned expressions and verify unsigned key interpretation.

edge: Place the unknown in the most-significant or least-significant bit.
negative: Read or write using indices containing X and Z.
positive: Use a fully known logic index.

edge: Use an empty or multi-byte string literal.
positive: Index with a string literal and with its equivalent packed byte vector and verify key identity.
